why: THE MOVED-CLAIM CORPUS, the refuter's positive and negative controls. Two audits of a strong model's freehand work on a frozen claim. (a) BATCH 4 of the DS-DEF-2 clarity re-cut, 2026-09-13: eight pool auditors and eight adversaries read 93 changed faces and filed 21 CLAIM_MOVED rows; the journals are kit/_progress/wf_980caecf-038 (the audit) and wf_874f9ad9-605 (the repair). (b) THE POWER LEAF's claim-freeze audit, 2026-09-14, two Opus readers merged over 189 re-cut spines: 32 moved claims, classed CERTAINTY 11, scope 5, added fact 5, dropped fact 5, quantity 4, tense 2 (kit/rewrite/clarity-audit-POW.md). `moved` is the offending text the model wrote; `repaired` is the line that landed or the audit's ruled FIX. A refuter that convicts `moved` and clears `repaired` has caught the class; one that convicts both has caught nothing and refused a good line.
